question.text: Under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) governed by FEMA 1999, what is the maximum amount an Indian resident individual can remit abroad per financial year for permissible current or capital account transactions?

explanation.text: The Logic: Resident individuals can freely remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year for permissible current or capital account transactions under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme. The scheme started at USD 25,000 and the ceiling has been revised in stages to reach the current level. The Trap: Lower figures such as USD 100,000 and USD 150,000 are earlier-stage limits or distractors and not the workbook-stated current ceiling. The USD 250,000 figure is the source-stated per-financial-year LRS limit. Note: Source basis is p.255 of the NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook (June 2025), which records the USD 2,50,000 per financial year LRS limit and notes the staged revisions from the original USD 25,000.
